answer: Each agent must lock a scarce, nontransferable credential in a public vault before it can earn fees; the credential is issued only after an in-person check by randomly selected local witnesses, whose own credentials are slashed if they attest to a duplicate. A ferrous token can mark the check-in device, but it is the witness bond and audit trail, not the token, that makes copying costly. To flood the reef of markets with fake identities, an attacker must recruit real witnesses and risk losing their locked stake for every detected lie.
